scope: Primary sources rechecked for Ch43. Workload numbers and custom catalog/GC/replay contracts remain teaching assumptions.

sources.title: Dremel: Interactive Analysis of Web-Scale Datasets (2010)
sources.location: Section 7, Figure 8 and MR and Dremel / Figure 10
sources.supports: T1 has 85 billion records and 87 TB uncompressed; Q1 reads roughly 0.5 TB compressed with Dremel/MR on columns versus 87 TB with MR on records.
sources.pageClaim: Historical byte ratios illustrate that scan bytes and execution time are different quantities; no latency transfer to A3.
sources.method: Google primary landing page via web; PDF tool access failed, then original PDF fetched with curl and inspected with pdftotext. Figure 9 is local-disk access; corrected the page to Figure 10.

sources.title: Column-Stores vs. Row-Stores: How Different Are They Really? (2008)
sources.supports: Physical column layout alone does not provide the full execution benefits; compression, block processing and late materialization contribute.
sources.pageClaim: Splitting every row-store column into a table does not itself implement a complete column-oriented execution engine.

sources.title: Apache Parquet File Format
sources.location: File Format, file layout and reader description
sources.supports: Column chunks belong to row groups; file metadata records their locations and readers use it to find selected chunks.
sources.pageClaim: Projected reads use metadata to locate required columns, including predicate columns.

sources.title: Apache Iceberg 1.10.0 Evolution
sources.supports: Stable field IDs preserve schema meaning; old and new partition layouts coexist, are planned separately, and evolution does not eagerly rewrite old files.
sources.pageClaim: Updating the default partition specification is distinct from physically rewriting historical layout.
sources.method: Version-pinned official documentation opened through web; not described as latest.

sources.title: Apache Iceberg 1.10.0 Reliability
sources.location: Concurrent write operations / Cost of retries / Retry validation
sources.supports: Writers atomically exchange table metadata pointers, refresh after conflicts and validate operation assumptions before reapplying actions.
sources.pageClaim: CAS alone does not validate stale compaction output. Atomic batch-result registration is this chapter's custom Catalog contract, not an Iceberg API guarantee.
sources.method: Version-pinned official documentation opened through web.

sources.title: Apache Iceberg Table Specification, v2-scoped claims
sources.location: Sequence Numbers / Row-level Deletes / Scan Planning / File System Operations
sources.supports: Data and metadata files remain immutable; v2 position/equality delete files have scope and sequence applicability that readers must honor.
sources.pageClaim: A snapshot's data files alone do not define correct live rows; applicable delete metadata must participate in planning/reading.
sources.method: Living official specification opened through web. Newer v3/v4 features are outside this chapter's v2 illustration.

sources.title: Apache Iceberg 1.10.0 Maintenance
sources.location: Expire snapshots / Remove orphan files / Compact data files
sources.supports: Rewriting small files reduces metadata and file-open cost; overly short orphan retention can delete in-progress files.
sources.pageClaim: 512 MB and 30 minutes are teaching values. Reachability, active readers and writer lifetime must be coordinated before cleanup.
sources.method: Version-pinned official documentation opened through web. Reader-pin/publication-fence protocol is a stated design contract rather than a claimed built-in maintenance API.

sources.title: Lakehouse: A New Generation of Open Platforms that Unify Data Warehousing and Advanced Analytics (2021)
sources.supports: Lakehouse combines low-cost directly accessible open files with data-management capabilities.
sources.pageClaim: Temperature, physical layout and storage medium are separate design axes; A4 prices are illustrative.
sources.method: Original conference paper opened through web.

sources.title: Jay Kreps, Questioning the Lambda Architecture (2014)
sources.location: Reprocessing steps and per-partition offset description
sources.supports: A new processor can replay retained input into a separate output table, catch up and then switch the application to it.
sources.pageClaim: Isolated replay avoids adding history to live aggregates; half-open next-offset definitions and recoverable cutover barriers are explicit chapter contracts.
sources.method: Original author's article opened through web.

sources.title: Amazon S3 User Guide: What is Amazon S3?
sources.location: Storage classes / Amazon S3 data consistency model
sources.supports: S3 offers differing access classes, strong object read-after-write consistency and atomic single-key updates, without atomic cross-key updates.
sources.pageClaim: Object medium alone does not determine access latency; object consistency cannot replace a table-level publication boundary.
sources.method: Official user guide opened through web.
